resources.string: The app uses accessibility service to listen for a duress password on the lockscreen. When found, it can send a broadcast message or wipe the device.
The length has to be at least your PIN/password length plus two.

If you use PIN/password (not the length), Keyguard A requires display password characters as you type option to be enabled. Keyguard B may be language dependent (EN). If you change Keyguard type, restart accessibility service.
Listening for the duress PIN on the lock screen
Tap to start listening on the lock screen
Send a broadcast to another app, e.g. Wasted, which then locks or wipes the device.
Factory reset the device without asking. All data will be lost. Requires device admin permission.
Only show a notification. Use it to check that the duress PIN is recognized before enabling wipe.
Which intent to send. Take the values from the receiving app.

If the app was installed from a file, open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then enable Duress in Accessibility → Installed apps. Samsung Auto Blocker in maximum restrictions mode blocks the service.

Turn on the Duress service in Accessibility.

If the switch is greyed out and says "Restricted setting" (the app was installed from an APK):
1. Tap the switch once and close the message.
2. Open App info, tap ⋮ in the top right corner and choose "Allow restricted settings".
3. Come back to Accessibility and turn Duress on.

On Samsung, if the ⋮ item is missing, check Settings → Security and privacy → Auto Blocker.
